output.brief:
The wrong expiry dates did not come from the agency operators or the printer firmware. Printer records show that from 4 Oct every Veltranol job received a 36-month shelf life from PackBridge, with no operator override. Before that, every job used 24 months, including jobs run by agency operators after the firmware change. The ERP record shows that on 3 Oct Regulatory Affairs entered a 36-month value for Veltranol, valid only from March 2027. The 24-month value is still the one in effect. PackBridge appears to have used the future-dated value anyway, which contradicts the vendor's statement that it can't. Two of the faulty lots came from Line 1 day shift, run by permanent staff. That rules out a night-shift or agency explanation. The camera passes the cartons because it only checks them against the job data.

What to do:
- Don't discipline or remove the agency operators.
- Keep the camera check on.
- Fix the Veltranol shelf-life record in the ERP.
- Hold every Veltranol lot packed since 4 Oct, including the two in the warehouse.
- Add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record at each setup.
- Check retained cartons of the two other products with future-dated edits (HX-15-30 and MR-05-14).
- Ask Corvane to explain why PackBridge used a future-dated value.

I'm fairly confident in this. Whether other products are affected is still unknown.
